words.concise_meaning: showing contempt for what is holy or sacred.
misconceptions: thinking it only means not religious
confusing it with being just plain rude

words.concise_meaning: having no connection to religion; worldly or civil.

semantic_axes.description: ranges from neutral indifference (secular) to active defiance/contempt (profane).
ranges from purely civil/worldly (secular) to explicitly violating the religious boundary (profane).

edge.boundary_rule: use profane when the actor actively violates or mocks a sacred boundary; use secular when they merely operate outside a religious framework.

misconceptions.M2: assuming profane only means bad language

profane: The spray-painting of the altar was a truly profane act.
His speech was filled with profane remarks about the church service.
They treated the holy relics in a deliberately profane manner.
The protesters performed a profane dance outside the temple.
It was seen as a profane misuse of the consecrated space.
The critic made several profane jokes during the religious play.
secular: The school offers a secular curriculum for all students.
They chose a secular venue for their wedding ceremony.
The government is committed to a strictly secular policy.
He works for a secular non-profit organization.
Many modern nations have a secular legal system.
She prefers to read books on secular philosophy.

profane: The school offers a profane curriculum for all students. (Incorrect)
They chose a profane venue for their wedding. (Incorrect)
The government is committed to a profane policy. (Incorrect)
He works for a profane non-profit. (Incorrect)
Many nations have a profane legal system. (Incorrect)
She prefers to read books on profane philosophy. (Incorrect)
secular: The spray-painting of the altar was a truly secular act. (Incorrect)
His speech was filled with secular remarks about the service. (Incorrect)
They treated the relics in a deliberately secular manner. (Incorrect)
The protesters performed a secular dance outside the temple. (Incorrect)
It was seen as a secular misuse of the space. (Incorrect)
The critic made several secular jokes during the play. (Incorrect)

borderline.text: The public library is an explicitly ___ space, where religion is neither taught nor expected.
borderline.note: It is not inherently anti-religious, just non-religious.

borderline.text: The comedian's act, which mocked the fundamental tenets of the faith, was considered highly ___.
borderline.note: The active mockery makes it more than just non-religious.

borderline.text: A ___ state ensures all religions are treated equally by not adopting any as its official doctrine.
borderline.note: This is a standard description of a neutral government.

borderline.text: By wearing shoes in the inner sanctum, the tourist committed a ___ breach of etiquette.
borderline.note: It violates the sanctity of the holy area, even if unintentionally.

chains.frame: The official policy of the town council regarding the new public square: ___

beats.text: The council decided to remove all religious symbols from the square.
beats.reason: It's about creating a neutral space.

beats.text: The square is now used only for city meetings.
beats.reason: This reinforces the non-religious nature.

chains.feedback_short: It stays secular because the policy is consistently non-religious and neutral, never disrespectful.
chains.feedback_deep: Removing religious symbols to create neutrality is a secular action. Using the space for civil meetings reinforces that neutrality without mocking anyone.
chains.contrast_rule: Secular space creation is not profane.
chains.hint: Is there any sign of mockery?

chains.frame: The performer's song choice for the memorial concert: ___

beats.text: The singer performed a song about lost love, not a hymn.
beats.reason: A song about love is simply not religious.

beats.text: The singer mocked the mourners and sang vulgar lyrics.
beats.reason: This shows direct disrespect.

chains.feedback_short: It flips because singing vulgar lyrics and mocking mourners is actively disrespectful, not just non-religious.
chains.feedback_deep: A secular choice is a non-religious alternative. A profane choice is a deliberate attempt to violate the sanctity or respectfulness of the event.
chains.contrast_rule: Disrespectful action is profane; non-religious action is secular.
chains.hint: Does the action violate the sanctity?

chains.frame: The university professor's approach to the topic of creation myths in his class: ___

beats.text: The professor treated them as literary artifacts, not literal truth.
beats.reason: Academic analysis is a non-religious approach.

beats.text: He analyzed them without any theological bias.
beats.reason: This confirms a neutral, academic approach.

chains.feedback_short: It narrows towards secular as the description of neutral, academic analysis confirms the lack of bias, not disrespect.
chains.feedback_deep: The professor's approach is secular, as he treats the material with objective academic distance, which is not disrespectful.
chains.hint: Is there any attempt to undermine or mock?

chains.frame: The artist's painting of the religious icon: ___

beats.text: The artist painted the figure with modern, everyday clothing.
beats.reason: Reinterpreting icons in a worldly context is secular.

beats.text: The artist clearly intended it to be a worldly representation.
beats.reason: This confirms the focus is on the human/worldly aspect.

chains.feedback_short: It stays secular as the focus is on a worldly reinterpretation, which is non-religious but not disrespectful.
chains.feedback_deep: The artist is making a secular statement about the figure's humanity, which doesn't involve mockery or intent to violate sanctity.
chains.hint: Does it seek to humiliate or just recontextualize?

chains.frame: The speaker's use of religious terminology during the debate: ___

beats.text: The speaker used the terms in a purely legal context.
beats.reason: Using terms for legal purposes is secular.

beats.text: The speaker twisted the terms to mock the religion.
beats.reason: This turns a neutral usage into a disrespectful one.

chains.feedback_short: It flips because twisting the terms to mock the religion is disrespectful, unlike using them for legal purposes.
chains.feedback_deep: Using terminology in a non-religious, legal context is secular. Actively manipulating that terminology to mock the religion itself is profane.
chains.contrast_rule: Legal terminology usage is secular; mocking terminology usage is profane.
chains.hint: What is the goal of the language?

chains.frame: The historian's analysis of the era's economic reforms: ___

beats.text: The reforms were entirely focused on trade and taxes.
beats.reason: Economic reforms are worldly affairs.

beats.text: The reforms excluded any influence from the Church.
beats.reason: This confirms they were purely civil.

chains.feedback_short: It stays secular because the focus is on economic reforms that are non-religious, not disrespectful.
chains.feedback_deep: Economic reforms focused on trade and taxes are secular, as they exist in the worldly/civil realm. The exclusion of religious influence just confirms this characterization.
chains.hint: Is there any sign of malice towards the Church?

chains.frame: The scientist's explanation of human biology: ___

beats.text: The explanation focuses on genetic and evolutionary processes.
beats.reason: Scientific explanation is a non-religious framework.

beats.text: The scientist added that these processes prove there is no purpose to life, clearly mocking religious views.
beats.reason: The added mockery makes it profane.

chains.feedback_short: It flips because adding mockery of religious views transforms a neutral scientific explanation into a profane act.
chains.feedback_deep: A purely scientific explanation is secular. When the scientist explicitly uses that explanation to mock religious views, they cross the line into the profane.
chains.contrast_rule: Objective science is secular; mocking beliefs is profane.

chains.frame: The nature of the new magazine about everyday life: ___

beats.text: It covers cooking, fashion, and gardening.
beats.reason: These topics are worldly and non-religious.

beats.text: It completely ignores any religious commentary, focusing entirely on worldly interests.
beats.reason: This is a standard feature of non-religious media.

chains.feedback_short: It stays secular because focusing on worldly interests without commenting on religion is non-religious, not disrespectful.
chains.feedback_deep: The magazine's focus on everyday life and its lack of religious commentary are entirely secular, which just means worldly and non-religious.
chains.hint: Does it try to insult or simply ignore?

chains.frame: The manager's approach to the company's holiday celebration: ___

beats.text: He decided it would be a generic winter party.
beats.reason: Avoiding religion is standard for inclusive secular events.

beats.text: He deliberately used a holy symbol as a coaster to insult believers.
beats.decisive_clue: used holy symbol as coaster to insult
beats.reason: This is active desecration.

chains.feedback_short: It flips because using a holy symbol as a coaster to insult is actively disrespectful, unlike hosting a generic party.
chains.feedback_deep: A generic party is secular. Using a holy object as a coaster with the intent to insult believers is a clear act of desecration, which is profane.
chains.contrast_rule: Inclusivity is secular; desecration is profane.
chains.hint: What does the symbol usage show?

chains.frame: The town's new policy on using the park for local events: ___

beats.text: The policy requires all events to be non-religious in nature.
beats.reason: This is a civil, neutral restriction.

beats.text: The park remains a neutral ground for any civil activity.
beats.reason: Neutrality in a public space is secular.

chains.feedback_short: It stays secular because the policy is consistently non-religious and aims for neutrality, not disrespect.
chains.feedback_deep: A policy restricting events to non-religious activities is a standard secular, civil measure aimed at maintaining neutral ground in public space.

chains.frame: Maya's attitude towards her partner's family traditions: ___

beats.text: She respectfully declines to participate, as she is not a believer.
beats.reason: Non-participation due to different beliefs is secular.

beats.text: She told the family that their traditions were utterly stupid and a waste of time.
beats.decisive_clue: called traditions stupid and a waste of time
beats.reason: Mockery shows disrespect.

chains.feedback_short: It flips because mocking the family's traditions is actively disrespectful, whereas respectfully declining to participate is simply a personal choice.
chains.feedback_deep: Declining participation for personal reasons is secular. Calling traditions stupid is active disrespect, making it profane.
chains.contrast_rule: Respectful difference is secular; mocking difference is profane.
chains.hint: How does she express her disagreement?

chains.frame: The nature of the local football club's foundation: ___

beats.text: The club was founded as a purely community-driven social activity.
beats.reason: A sports club is inherently secular.

beats.text: They operate entirely without any religious affiliation or goals.
beats.reason: Non-religious is secular.

chains.feedback_short: It stays secular because a community-driven club with no religious affiliation is simply non-religious, not disrespectful.
chains.feedback_deep: A sports club is a classic example of a secular organization—it's worldly, community-focused, and non-religious.

chains.frame: The tourist's behavior while visiting the temple: ___

beats.text: The tourist spoke loudly and touched the sacred statues.
beats.decisive_clue: spoke loudly and touched sacred statues
beats.reason: This is disrespectful to a sacred space.

beats.text: They clearly had no idea they were violating any rules.
beats.reason: It's still profane, just not malicious.

chains.feedback_short: It stays profane, even if unintentional, because they still violated the sacred boundary.
chains.feedback_deep: Even if the tourist is unaware of the rules, their actions (touching statues in a sacred space) are still objectively profane because they violate the sanctity.
chains.contrast_rule: Violating sanctity is profane, intentional or not.
chains.hint: Does it matter if they knew the rules?

chains.frame: The family's practice of using a special, old box for storing board games: ___

beats.text: They bought it at a yard sale, totally unaware of its past.
beats.reason: It's just an ordinary item.

beats.text: They were later told it was once used for religious relics, and they chose to continue using it for games anyway, mocking the idea of its history.
beats.reason: This makes the choice disrespectful.

chains.feedback_short: It reframes to profane when they explicitly mock the relic's history, changing their action from indifferent to disrespectful.
chains.feedback_deep: The initial use was secular (indifferent). Once they learn the history and mock it, the action becomes profane.
chains.hint: Does their attitude change after learning the history?

chains.frame: The judge's ruling on the oath-taking ceremony: ___

beats.text: The judge allowed for non-religious affirmations as an alternative.
beats.reason: Allowing non-religious options is secular.

beats.text: He emphasized that the legal system must be independent of all religious oaths.
beats.reason: This is a key component of secularism.

chains.feedback_short: It narrows towards secular as the emphasis on legal independence from religious oaths confirms a principled approach, not disrespect.
chains.feedback_deep: Creating a legal path for secular (non-religious) affirmation is a principled secular measure, not an act of disrespect (profane).
chains.hint: Is there any attempt to undermine religion?

chains.frame: The novelist's depiction of the priesthood in his latest book: ___

beats.text: He writes them as ordinary, flawed people in a modern, worldly setting.
beats.reason: Humanizing is worldly/secular.

beats.text: He uses them to justify immoral actions, explicitly mocking the religious ideals they once stood for.
beats.reason: This is direct disrespect.

chains.feedback_short: It corrupts to profane when the depiction moves from humanizing flaws to explicitly mocking the religious ideals themselves.
chains.feedback_deep: Humanizing is a secular, worldly approach. Using the characters to justify immorality while mocking the religious ideals they represent is profane.
chains.contrast_rule: Humanizing is secular; mocking ideals is profane.
chains.hint: Does he just show their flaws or mock their ideals?

beats.text: The clothes are designed for comfort and everyday practicality.
beats.reason: Practical, everyday fashion is worldly/secular.

beats.text: It features modern, non-traditional styles for everyday wear.
beats.reason: Non-traditional and worldly is secular.

chains.feedback_short: It stays secular because modern, everyday fashion is worldly and non-religious, not disrespectful.
chains.feedback_deep: Fashion designed for comfort and everyday use is worldly, making the design philosophy secular. It does not touch upon or mock religion.

chains.frame: The chef's interpretation of a traditional religious meal: ___

beats.text: He adapted it for a modern diet, removing certain ingredients.
beats.reason: This is a practical, worldly adaptation.

beats.text: He added meat to the dish and served it while mocking the religious observers.
beats.reason: This turns a practical adaptation into mockery.

chains.feedback_short: It flips because mocking the religious observers makes a dietary adaptation profane, whereas adapting for a modern diet is just secular.
chains.feedback_deep: Adapting a recipe for a diet is a secular (worldly/practical) act. Mocking religious observers while doing so makes the act profane.
chains.contrast_rule: Practical adaptation is secular; mockery is profane.
chains.hint: Why did he add the forbidden ingredient?

chains.frame: The reason the organization gave for focusing on climate change instead of theology: ___

beats.text: They stated they want to focus on worldly, empirical solutions.
beats.reason: Empirical is a non-religious framework.

beats.text: They argued that empirical evidence is all that matters.
beats.decisive_clue: empirical evidence is all that matters
beats.reason: This is a classic secular stance.

chains.feedback_short: It uses secular because the focus is on empirical, worldly evidence, which is non-religious but not disrespectful.
chains.feedback_deep: Focusing on worldly, empirical solutions is a secular (non-religious) stance. It does not imply malice or disrespect toward religion.
chains.hint: Does it reject or simply not prioritize?
